gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-serif-thai: Gugi draws every curve and stem with one constant line width, like bent cable, and its tall lowercase nearly touches the capitals. Noto Serif Thai follows with sturdy thin lines and slightly heavier thick ones, a mellow serif that settles into long reading.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-serif-tibetan: Gugi cuts its strokes like a router bit with a fixed width, leaving terminals open so the counters flow outward. Noto Serif Tibetan, a classic serif, counters with quiet stems.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-serif-todhri: Noto Serif Todhri is a text serif whose thinnest curve points still carry real weight, with a sizable x-height made for screens. Gugi sits above it with no swelling or thinning at all, like cable bent into shapes.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-serif-toto: Dignified Noto Serif Toto has a hulking lowercase, like thick chalk pressed hard, with subtle thick and thin modulation. Gugi, drawn like bent wire in round letters, looks lighter and more playful beside it, while the text serif stays literary.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-serif-vithkuqi: Noto Serif Vithkuqi is a text serif with big round lowercase bowls and stems a touch heavier than its crossbars. Gugi gives blueprint-style constant lines for headings; the body handles sustained text.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-serif-yezidi: Noto Serif Yezidi forms words as solid blocks, not skylines. Gugi is best at bold, constant-stroke display lines like bent wire, while this text serif is best at light verticals-to-curves contrast over paragraphs.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-odor-mean-chey: Dignified Odor Mean Chey squeezes the mouths of its a, e and s into tall rounded forms, a classic serif with editorial poise. And Gugi, with bowls and stems drawn at the same weight, gives the headline a bolder, plainly built front.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-pt-serif-caption: PT Serif Caption has a clearly tall x-height and slightly thinner joins where curves meet stems, yet every stroke stays solid. Gugi, like cable bent into shapes, leads, and the serif below would carry a long page gently.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-suez-one: Bookish Suez One looks closed and compact, with a thin channel into each counter, while Gugi's open letters flow outward. As a classic serif, it would hold a long read with a refined, dense texture.
gen-gf-gugi-lora: Gugi's tall lowercase nearly reaches its capitals, with terminals cut open so the counters flow outward and bold. Gugi excels at striking display lines, while Lora, a classic serif, does its best work as literary body text.
